brief.headline: Close the ₹8.48 L price gap on PET bottles to match our best price — we already pay ₹7.62/NOS at TPAC, and the open market sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc, so there's clear room to drop PIK's ₹8.49 rate

priceAsk.summary: Ask PIK to match the ₹7.62/NOS we pay TPAC Packaging for the amber 250ml PET bottle and close the 11.5% gap on that SKU
priceAsk.target: ₹8.48 L annual saving by moving to our best prices across their range
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹7.62/NOS to TPAC Packaging India Pvt Ltd. for the same PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM bottle that PIK charges ₹8.49/NOS — an 11.5% gap that costs us ₹7.19 L a year on that one item alone. The open-market ask for similar caps runs ₹0.85–0.95/pc (verdict: MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume), so PIK's pricing has room to come down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt — no extension

brief.financialLeverage: PIK Plastics publishes no public financials, so we can't see their profit, debt or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend is meaningful for a private converter, but without their revenue we can't pin the percentage. That means our leverage comes from the price gap we can prove — ₹8.48 L a year — and from the four credible alternates we've lined up (Mold-Tek, Manjushree, Hitech, Pearl). We can push firmly on price because we have fall-back sources, but we keep the payment term where it is since we don't know if faster payment would help them or cost us unnecessarily.

evidence.point: We pay PIK ₹8.49/NOS for the amber 250ml PET bottle
TPAC Packaging supplies the same bottle at ₹7.62/NOS — 11.5% cheaper
That single SKU costs us an extra ₹7.19 L a year
Total annual price overpay across PIK's range is ₹8.48 L
Open-market asking price for similar caps is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
Our total annual spend with PIK is ₹1.92 Cr

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — top second-source candidate with proven scale and solid health

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed, ₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (manufacturer, India-Pan)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — resin/polymer maker with pan-India reach, medium confidence

risks: PIK's financials aren't public, so we can't see early-warning signs of trouble — watch their delivery performance and quality closely as we negotiate
If PIK digs in and won't move on price, be ready to RFQ Manjushree and Mold-Tek immediately — both are qualified alternates already on our books
The ₹8.48 L saving assumes we can move all SKUs to best-price levels; PIK may argue tooling or spec differences on some items — ask for line-by-line proof

Market backups (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Srichakra, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are research leads, not qualified suppliers — treat them as long-term options to explore, not ready alternates for this meeting
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying you ₹8.49 a bottle for the amber 250ml PET when TPAC gives us the same item at ₹7.62 — let's talk about closing that 11.5% gap and bringing your pricing in line with what we already pay elsewhere.
